_about: Deterministic job filters. Title keywords match whole words on a normalized title: lowercase, no accents, 'back-end'/'back end' -> 'backend', 'full-stack' -> 'fullstack', 'front-end' -> 'frontend', 'Sr.' -> 'senior', plurals of engineer/developer folded. After editing, run `jobhunter reclassify` to re-apply to stored jobs.
_max_posting_age_days: Two weeks, for every source, company careers pages and the visa list included (only a --from/--to date range asks for older jobs): watched boards read whole careers pages, which keep postings up for months. Measured from posting to when the job was found.
_senior: Senior roles (the user's call 2026-11-20, after ~300 applications and 1 interview): any target role is rejected, code too_senior, quoted, when its title has a word from title_words or its text asks for a senior person ('We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer', 'Position level: Senior', 'senior-level expertise'; relevance.py). Only naming senior colleagues ('work with senior engineers', 'junior and senior welcome') is kept. With reject_if_required_yoe_at_least 5 (was 6), a stated 5+ years is rejected too.
_blocked_companies: Companies you never want shortlisted again. Rejected before any other rule, with the reason quoted. Matched on the normalized company name (Inc, Ltd, .com etc. ignored).

_agencies: Staffing agencies and talent marketplaces: they repost other companies' jobs, sell vetted developers or pay per task. Rejected (code agency) with what matched: a name below, a whole word in the company name, or a phrase in the posting. not_agencies: real companies a name word would catch. Checked against the stored jobs 2026-10-10: 'our clients', 'talent pool' and 'talent network' are left out because real companies (Zscaler, Percona, GitLab) use them.
_relocation: Countries you would move to. A job there may be on-site or hybrid (elsewhere only remote counts); 'Remote (UAE)' counts too, since it means living there. Rejected only when the posting wants nationals or people already there (title_local_only, local_only; quoted), or pays under RELOCATION_MIN_MONTHLY_USD in .env. sponsor: the sentence is quoted as a good sign. ask_about: quoted as a note, not a rejection. Matched as whole words, any case. From research 2026-10-10 (docs/research).

local_only: must be residing in the UAE

_gulf_remote: Gulf countries you want the companies of, but would not move to: Kuwait and Bahrain (your call 2026-11-13). The opposite of `relocation` above. Only a REMOTE job listed there counts, and it is never shortlisted on evidence: it is kept `unclear` (code gulf_remote), quoting the location, so the daily AI check asks whether they can hire someone living in Lebanon and rejects it with a quote when they cannot. On-site or hybrid there is rejected like anywhere else (not_remote); a posting that wants someone already in the country is rejected (local_only), by the general wording in the shared `relocation.local_only` and `title_local_only` lists ("National only", "transferable visa", "no visa sponsorship") - their UAE and Qatar phrases never match here, and a rule naming the country itself ("must be based in Kuwait") is caught by eligibility's description rules; a location that also names another place ("Kuwait or India") is rejected as before (location_restricted); and an AI check that says cannot_hire while only quoting the location back is not used, since the rules kept the job knowing where it is listed. src/jobhunter/gulf.py.
_visa_list: Countries you would move to on a work visa. A target role there (on-site, hybrid, or remote for people living there) goes to the separate visa list (status visa_list) only with evidence the employer sponsors visas, quoted: the posting offers one, a Hacker News header says VISA, or the company is on that country's government sponsor list (uk, nl, ie: data/sponsors/, `jobhunter sponsors --update`, refreshed by the daily run every refresh_days). Also kept: a role The Stack lists, or a company on JobDelulu's sponsor list (sponsor_sites.py, the user's call 2026-11-16), and in `silent_ok` countries a posting that says nothing either way. Rejected, quoted: the posting refuses or wants a right to work you don't have (no_sponsor), asks for or is written in one of `languages` (language_required: your profile lists Arabic and English only), or says nothing (no_visa_evidence). The phrases are in src/jobhunter/visa.py. Places in a location that also names a US state or the US are skipped ('Dublin, OH'), and one naming Canada, Australia or New Zealand counts as that country ('London, Ontario' is Canada); 'Cambridge' (MA), 'Wales' (New South Wales) and 'England' (New England) are left out; London, UK and United Kingdom cover them. Researched 2026-10-13 (docs/research).

The fit score's visa part ranks these low unless the company has other evidence.

_title_include: A title must contain at least one of these, or be an AI engineering role: 'AI', 'LLM', 'GenAI' or 'Agentic' followed within three words by engineer/developer ('AI Harness Engineer'; relevance.py). Lead titles (Technical Lead, Engineering Lead) are left out on purpose: when they state years, most ask for 5+ (checked 2026-10-19).
_title_include_needs_role: Keywords from title_include that only count when the title also names an engineering role (engineer, developer, programmer, swe). "Forward Deployed Engineer" passes; "Forward-Deployed Banker" and "Forward Deployed AI Scientist" are not target roles (title_not_target). The user's call, 2026-11-06: both were skipped by hand as not-my-role.
_junior_only: AI and forward-deployed roles you apply to only at junior level (decision 2026-10-20, see docs/decisions.md; backend, software and solutions roles keep the years rules above). A title is one when it has a word from `roles` or is an AI engineering role (relevance.py), unless it also names one of `unless_title_names` ('Senior Python / AI Backend Engineer' is a backend role). Rejected (code junior_only), quoted: a word from `title_words` in the title, or a stated years ask at or above reject_if_required_yoe_at_least. The years can be in any field ('3+ years of software, 1+ with LLMs' counts as 3). No years stated is kept.
_title_exclude: Seniority and job-function words. Any of these rejects the title, with no exceptions.
_title_exclude_single_role: Specialties. Rejected, unless the title also names a target role: 'Frontend / Backend Engineer' passes.
_title_exclude_unless_python: A role built on another language. Rejected unless the title also says Python.
_other_stack: A role built on another language that the title doesn't name (the user's call 2026-11-26, after 195 skips with the reason 'Wrong stack'; the title rule above only sees 'Backend Engineer (Java)'). Rejected, code other_stack, quoting the sentence, when the posting names none of `yours` anywhere (any case; React, Go, Rust, Ruby and Rails only as written) and requires one of `others` in a sentence that is no bonus, choice or thing to learn ('C++ is a plus', 'Java or a comparable language', 'willingness to work in Go' never count; relevance.py). 'Go' counts only as a language: 'in Go', 'Kotlin / Go'. Checked against the stored jobs 2026-11-26: 46 of the 195 wrong-stack skips, 12 of 342 applied jobs (all built on Java, Go, C# or .NET), 3 of the 58 in To apply.
_fit_weights: Points per skill found in the posting, based on profile/master_profile.md. Only used to sort the report.
